title: Algebraic naturality of the localized base-derived tensor comparison
statement: Let $R,A,B,D$ be commutative rings, with $R$-algebra structures on $A,B$ and an $(A\otimes_R B)$-algebra structure on $D$ [def-weil-module-base-change, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Use derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of modules over all four rings. Let $P,Q$ be cochain complexes of $A$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], and $M,N$ base-derived tensor cohomology models [def-pc-base-derived-tensor-cohomology-model] for $P,Q$ with coefficients $B,D$. Let $L:D(A)\to D(D)$ with universal left-derived counit $\epsilon$ derive extension along $A\to A\otimes_R B\to D$, and suppose $\epsilon_P,\epsilon_Q$ are invertible. Write $s_P:H^i(L(Q(P)))\cong H^i(P\otimes_A D)$ and $s_Q$ for the counit isomorphisms including the specified localization factors. Let $a:Q(P)\cong Q(Q)$ be an isomorphism in $D(A)$ and $i\in\mathbf Z$. Define $v:M_i\cong N_i$ as a B-linear isomorphism by exact restriction of $a$ from A to R, the localization-factor identifications of the model inputs, applying M.derived, the unique counit-compatible natural isomorphism M.derived to N.derived, applying degree-i homology, and the two model cohomology identifications. For every $(A\otimes_R B)$-linear isomorphism $e:M_i\cong N_i$ whose restriction to B is v, the equality $M.c_i;s_P^{-1};H^i(L(a))=(D\otimes_{A\otimes_R B}e);N.c_i;s_Q^{-1}$ holds as a D-linear equality. Here c denotes localizedComparison. There is no flatness, K-flatness or invertibility hypothesis on c.

proof.text: Derived tensor functoriality and the coefficient-extension chain map give the natural comparison from base-derived tensor after exact restriction to derived A-to-D extension. Choose K-flat resolutions to construct the comparison and descend through localization. Its naturality is for arbitrary derived A-linear morphisms, not just chain maps.

The unique counit-compatible isomorphism between the models identifies the source transport with baseTensorSourceIso. Apply homology. The equations comparison_eq and the generator formulas for ordinaryIso and ordinaryToLocalized identify the model maps with the canonical comparison.

Use localized_eq and extension/restriction adjunction to transpose the preceding naturality square. Restriction to B is faithful, so the given e is the prescribed tensor-algebra transport. Conjugate the targets by the scalarExtensionHomologyIso from the invertible counits.
